arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Fisher stated the Confrontation Clause protects against trial by affidavit.
Schertler argued the Confrontation Clause does not apply to machine-generated results.
Coakley claimed the drug certificates are not testimonial statements.
Kennedy questioned if a lab report is distinct from a police report.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: Jeffrey Fisher argues the Confrontation Clause bans trial by affidavit. He says the right to confront witnesses is core to fair trials. The state argues the report is a machine-generated result. It is not a witness statement. The state says the defendant can call the analyst if needed. This avoids forcing the state to produce the analyst.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the scope of the right to confront witnesses. It determines whether lab reports require live testimony. The outcome affects how prosecutors prove scientific evidence in criminal trials. It shapes the balance between trial efficiency and defendant rights.
